clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old male presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain, afebrile, hypertensive, and with RLQ tenderness. Initial workup shifted towards pulmonary concerns, leading to a pulmonary ventilation and perfusion (V/Q) scan, which was ordered due to concerns about contrast nephrotoxicity after a recent nephrectomy. The V/Q scan revealed findings suggestive of a pulmonary embolus. A chest CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) was subsequently ordered to confirm the diagnosis of massive saddle PE, but the specific results of this CTPA were not documented in the provided reports.
